description: WS-TRNX-TABLE AT ITS FIRST ELEMENT - the 1-based-to-0-based subscript conversion, which gate G33 requires be asserted at both ends of the table: this case owns the first element and case08 owns the last. OCCURS appears 27 times across the 28 programs and is the single largest source of off-by-one defects in this migration, because a COBOL subscript starts at 1 and a Java index starts at 0. The correspondence is therefore stated here explicitly rather than left implied (practice B8): COBOL WS-CARD-NUM (1) is Java index [0], and COBOL WS-TRAN-NUM (1, 1) is Java [0][0]. THE SUBJECT'S SHAPE: app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:L225-L233 declares 01 WS-TRNX-TABLE as 05 WS-CARD-TBL OCCURS 51 TIMES holding 10 WS-CARD-NUM PIC X(16) and 10 WS-TRAN-TBL OCCURS 10 TIMES holding 15 WS-TRAN-NUM PIC X(16) and 15 WS-TRAN-REST PIC X(318) - a 51 x 10 TWO-dimensional table, which is the fourth of the five features the program header advertises at :L34 - and it declares, SEPARATELY, 01 WS-TRN-TBL-CNTR as 05 WS-TRN-TBL-CTR OCCURS 51 TIMES holding 10 WS-TRCT PIC S9(4) COMP. The counter array is a parallel OCCURS 51 in its own 01 item, not a third dimension of the first and not a member of it, and it is preserved that way rather than merged for tidiness (practice B5). The geometry is arithmetic from the PICTURE clauses, not an estimate (practice B11): one card slot is 16 + 10 x (16 + 318) = 3,356 bytes, so the whole table is 51 x 3,356 = 171,156 bytes, and WS-TRAN-REST X(318) is exactly the width of app/cpy/COSTM01.CPY's TRNX-REST, whose own items sum 2 + 4 + 10 + 100 + 11 + 9 + 50 + 50 + 10 + 26 + 26 = 298 plus a trailing FILLER X(20) = 318. Both 01 items are cleared together by INITIALIZE WS-TRNX-TABLE WS-TRN-TBL-CNTR at :L294, before the first file is opened. WHAT THE FIRST ELEMENT PINS: 8100-TRNXFILE-OPEN primes the subscripts before any row is stored - MOVE TRNX-CARD-NUM TO WS-SAVE-CARD, MOVE 1 TO CR-CNT, MOVE 0 TO TR-CNT (:L757-L759) - so when 8500-READTRNX-READ runs its card-break test at :L819 the saved card equals the record's card and the ADD 1 TO TR-CNT arm is taken, giving CR-CNT = 1 and TR-CNT = 1. The three stores at :L827-L829 therefore address WS-CARD-NUM (1), WS-TRAN-NUM (1, 1) and WS-TRAN-REST (1, 1) - in Java [0], [0][0] and [0][0]. The sequential read at :L835 then reports end of file, the '10' arm at :L841 leaves the loop, and 8599-EXIT's MOVE TR-CNT TO WS-TRCT (CR-CNT) at :L850 sets WS-TRCT (1) = 1 - the parallel array's first element, Java [0]. On the consuming side 1000-MAINLINE re-primes MOVE 1 TO CR-JMP at :L324 and 4000-TRNXFILE-GET's outer PERFORM VARYING CR-JMP FROM 1 BY 1 (:L417) and inner PERFORM VARYING TR-JMP FROM 1 BY 1 (:L422) BOTH start at 1, so the one transaction this run writes is the one reached at CR-JMP = 1, TR-JMP = 1. Reading either loop as starting at 0, or sizing either table at 50 or at 9, changes the record set this case pins and is exactly what it exists to catch. UNIT AND INVOCATION: statement.StatementGenerationJobA as a BATCH_JOB, reached at step/Tasklet level with statement.StatementGenerationJobB as its constructor-injected collaborator - no JobLauncher, no job repository and no HTTP anywhere in the path (gate G51). jobParameters is empty because no step of app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL carries a PARM; the only PARM in this estate is INTCALC.jcl's. No abend arm is reached, so expectedReturnCode is 0. SEED, DERIVED RATHER THAN INVENTED: TRNXFILE is inline because there is no tenth fixture - app/data/ASCII holds exactly nine .txt files and none of them is a statement transaction file - and the single row is not composed by hand either. It is app/data/ASCII/dailytran.txt row 20 (line 21), the FIRST row of that fixture whose card is 0500024453765740, put through STEP010's own projection: OUTREC FIELDS=(1:263,16,17:1,262,279:279,50) at CREASTMT.JCL:54 moves the 16-byte card number from offset 263 to the front, follows it with the 262 bytes from TRNX-ID through TRNX-MERCHANT-ZIP, and then copies 50 bytes from 279 - which is why TRNX-ORIG-TS arrives whole as 2022-06-10 19:27:53.000000 while TRNX-PROC-TS, blank in the source row, arrives blank. CVTRA06Y and CVTRA05Y share every width and offset, so the positions the SORT names land on the same spans. The result is exactly 350 bytes - TRNX-CARD-NUM X(16) plus TRNX-ID X(16) as the 32-byte composite key that DELDEF01 corroborates with KEYS(32 0) at :30 and RECORDSIZE(350 350) at :32, then TRNX-REST's 318 - and its trailing FILLER X(20) is emitted as spaces, which the declared total width proves (gate G21). Rows must be ascending by card then id, the order SORT FIELDS=(263,16,CH,A,1,16,CH,A) at :53 produces; with one row that holds trivially, and it is the invariant a multi-row case would have to keep. The card number is cardxref.txt row 0's XREF-CARD-NUM verbatim, so the search at :L420 matches at the first element; its XREF-CUST-ID 000000050 and XREF-ACCT-ID 00000000050 drive the two keyed reads, which is why the statement is for Aniya Alba Von at ACCT-CURR-BAL 492.00 with FICO 623 and not for either master file's first row (practice B1). XREFFILE stays 36 bytes here: ParityCase.Normalisation is the sole owner of the 14-space pad up to CVACT03Y's declared 50 and applies it once, at seed time, so the fixture is never edited and the pad is never double-applied (gate G16). ACCTFILE and CUSTFILE are acctdata.txt (300 x 50) and custdata.txt (500 x 50) whole, the customer read through CUSTREC, whose date of birth is CUST-DOB-YYYYMMDD and never CVCUS01Y's CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD. COUNTS AND WIDTHS: with N = 1 transaction the run writes 19 + N = 20 STMTFILE records and 64 + 11N = 75 HTMLFILE records, at contiguous zero-based row indices in write order, and expectedDatasets pins both counts and both widths on the WRITES channel. STMTFILE is 80 bytes from two independent sources - 01 FD-STMTFILE-REC PIC X(80) at :L45 and CREASTMT.JCL LINE 89, DCB=(LRECL=80,BLKSIZE=8000,RECFM=FB), under the STMTFILE DD at line 87. Line 90 of that JCL is genuinely corrupted - verbatim '//         SPACE=(CYL,(1,1),RLSE), 00,RECFM=FB), ATA.VSAM.KSDS' - and its ' 00,RECFM=FB)' remnant sits directly beneath STMTFILE where it is easily misread as LRECL=100. Line 89 is the one cited, and the JCL is left exactly as it stands: it is the parity oracle, so the hazard is worked around here rather than corrected there (practice B4). HTMLFILE is 100 bytes from 01 FD-HTMLFILE-REC PIC X(100) at :L47 and from line 94, DCB=(LRECL=100,BLKSIZE=800,RECFM=FB), which supersedes STEP030's pre-delete LRECL=80 at line 69 because the step that creates the dataset wins (risk R-G). Each FD record is a single elementary item, so one addressable span is declared per dataset and every expectation pins that span by its whole image, which parity.FieldDiffer walks span by span rather than as one opaque string and which fixes the total width at the same time (gates G19, G20, G21). THE FIRST ELEMENT'S OWN BYTES: because CR-JMP = 1 and TR-JMP = 1 reach WS-TRAN-NUM (1, 1) and WS-TRAN-REST (1, 1), 6000-WRITE-TRANS renders that slot and no other. TRNX-ID 0000000058866561 becomes ST-TRANID X(16) at STMTFILE row 16 and the HTMLFILE row 58 cell; TRNX-DESC X(100) is truncated on the right into ST-TRANDT X(49) (:L677), so 'Purchase at Blick-Rippin' carries 25 trailing spaces into both row 16 and the row 61 cell, whose STRING operands are DELIMITED BY '*' and therefore copy the whole fixed-width span; and the seeded TRNX-AMT '0000001838H' is an 11-byte zoned S9(09)V99 closing on the +8 overpunch, so 183.88. ADD TRNX-AMT TO WS-TOTAL-AMT at :L429 is the only arithmetic on this path, WS-TOTAL-AMT PIC S9(9)V99 COMP-3 and WS-TRN-AMT PIC S9(9)V99 are both scale 2, and every amount is a BigDecimal at scale 2 with RoundingMode.DOWN - never HALF_UP, never HALF_EVEN, never double and never float - because ROUNDED appears zero times in all 28 programs, so COBOL truncates on store. ST-TRANAMT and ST-TOTAL-TRAMT PIC Z(9).99- render 183.88 as six spaces, 183, '.88' and a blank sign position, 13 bytes whose trailing position carries '-' only for a negative value, and the HTML amount cell receives that already-edited image rather than re-applying the mask (:L712). With one transaction the total equals the amount, so rows 16 and 18 carry the same 13 bytes. DETERMINISM AND ENCODING: nothing here is read from a clock. The program composes no timestamp of its own, and TRNX-ORIG-TS and TRNX-PROC-TS are seed bytes taken from the shipped fixture, never a 'now' (practice B7). Bytes are US-ASCII throughout, matching app/data/ASCII, and never a platform default (practice B8). PROVENANCE: every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of the CBSTM03A paragraphs and the ST-LINE and HTML templates, cross-checked against the COSTM01, CUSTREC, CVACT01Y and CVACT03Y byte layouts, the CREASTMT.JCL DD, DCB, SORT and IDCAMS contracts and the real ASCII fixtures. It was never captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy carries literal TAB characters that break parsing outright (practice B12, risk R-A). No user rules were provided for this project - review_rules returns exactly one line saying so - so the enterprise practices cited above stand in their place and the bar is not lowered.
